title: Quasi-affineness descends along an arbitrary field extension
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: If X_K is quasi-affine for some field extension K/k, the lemma concludes that X is quasi-affine (statement lines 2782-2786). The proof is the same spreading-out pattern as for properness: surjectivity of X_K to X gives quasi-compactness of X, and the quasi-separatedness of X is deduced by separating affine opens upstairs, so that X may be assumed quasi-compact and quasi-separated (proof lines 2789-2797). Then K is written as the colimit of its finitely generated k-subalgebras, X_K is recognized as the limit of the base changes X_i, and quasi-affineness descends to some X_i; a maximal ideal of that finitely generated algebra gives a finite extension k' by the Nullstellensatz, and since X_{k'} is a closed subscheme of X_i it is quasi-affine, whence X is quasi-affine by descent along the finite locally free morphism X_{k'} to X (proof lines 2800-2813). The claim is H2: four cited inputs arranged so that quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are available before the limit argument is applied.
